title: Multiplying needs a common denominator
statement: Before multiplying fractions you must write them with a common denominator, then multiply the numerators and keep the denominator.

evidence_patterns.item_shape: multiply two fractions with unlike denominators
evidence_patterns.signature: converts to a common denominator, multiplies numerators and keeps the common denominator

evidence_patterns.item_shape: multiply two fractions with like denominators
evidence_patterns.signature: multiplies numerators and keeps the shared denominator

discriminators.vs_slip: The extra common-denominator step is visible in the working and repeated across items. A slip does not add that step.

vs.math.frac.cross-multiply-to-multiply: Cross-multipliers do not convert denominators; they give 1/2 x 1/3 = (1x3)/(2x1) = 3/2.
vs.math.frac.add-across: Add-across is the mirror error (addition treated like multiplication). A learner with both answers 1/2 + 1/3 = 2/5 and 1/2 x 1/3 = 6/6.

conflicts_with.label: CCSS 5.NF.B.4: multiply a fraction or whole number by a fraction
